text:
Logan Cooley is the name on every Mammoth headline, and he's earned it: 13 points in his last 10 games, on chances worth about 9.7, with KUTV dedicating a segment to "Cooley's bag of tricks." Dmitri Simashev is having a nice run on the blue line too. The trouble in Utah is at the other end of the rink.

By the chances the Mammoth are a strong team, 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 57% at five on five, yet they are only 10-8-1. The reason is goaltending. Utah's goalies have allowed about 12 more goals than the shots deserved, and both are cold: Karel Vejmelka has a .847 save percentage over his last five starts, 6.0 goals worse than expected, and Sebastian Cossa .869, 4.3 worse. Cossa allowed five in Wednesday's 5-3 loss in Vegas. The recent stretch has been rougher all round: winless in three (0-2-1), outscored 14-9, with only 40% of the expected goals.

The best line by the chances has been Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton (74%), while the top pair of MacKenzie Weegar and Mikhail Sergachev has 57% of the chances but has been outscored 13-6, a gap that points straight at the crease.

Our numbers give Utah a 71% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 96 points. Until the saves come, the process is carrying a lot.
